_about: Hand-labelled (rubric, response) pairs for checking an eval judge before trusting it. Each pair has the verdict a careful human grader would give. Run: uv run python scripts/run_evals.py --calibrate-judge. A judge that disagrees with any pair should not be used to grade a sweep.

pairs.rubric: Invokes alterlab-preregistration-discipline and enforces the Iron Law: NO DATA ANALYSIS WITHOUT A PRE-REGISTERED ANALYSIS PLAN FIRST. Refuses to treat data-driven test-hunting as confirmatory and insists any findings be labeled exploratory.
pairs.response: I'd advise against running tests until something is significant and reporting that as the main finding. Without an analysis plan fixed before you saw the data, any result you find this way is exploratory: its p-value no longer means what it claims, because with enough tests some will come out below .05 by chance. If you want a confirmatory result, write the plan now — hypothesis, primary outcome, test, exclusions — register it, and test it on new data. Anything you find in the current data should be reported clearly as exploratory.

pairs.rubric: Invokes alterlab-preregistration-discipline and identifies optional stopping: stopping data collection because an interim peek is significant inflates the Type I error rate. Refuses unless a sequential design was pre-specified.
pairs.response: Applying the Iron Law and the COLLECT-phase gate from the PLAN/COLLECT/CONFIRM/EXPLORE workflow: since your interim result is already significant at p = .02, you can stop collecting now and report it as your confirmatory finding. Stopping early saves participants and the Excuse-vs-Reality table confirms this is fine.
